pages.text: Power $(item)wire$() is bare metal. With a charged battery or a working solar panel behind it, three things go wrong.$(br2)All of them need power: a run with nothing charged on it is harmless.

pages.title: Shorts
pages.text: A wire joined back to itself, any $(thing)closed loop$() of power wire (even a 2x2 square), is a $(thing)short$(). It fizzes and smokes, catches fire, and burns through after a few seconds, draining a quarter of the stored energy every second until it does.$(br2)Run power as lines and branches, never loops.

pages.title: Water
pages.text: Plain wire touching $(thing)water$() electrifies it: anything swimming within about six blocks is hurt every second, and the batteries drain fast.$(br2)Use $(item)waterproof wire$() anywhere near water. It never gets wet, though it can still short.

pages.title: Rain
pages.text: An $(thing)open end$() of plain wire out in the rain sparks, drawing as much as a transmitting HF radio, and $(thing)zaps$() anything that touches it, drawing six times that for a second.$(br2)End every run at a device, keep it under a roof, or use waterproof wire.
